title: run-epic must write its own durable run log
description:
When the epic-pwp run died mid-dispatch on 2026-09-14 there was no record of WHY. The process had been launched in the background with no stdout/stderr capture, so its last words went nowhere. The run feed showed tier_derived for gms and then silence; the attempt record for attempt 7 was written with a full job_handle (herdr had answered), but no workspace and no write ref were ever created. The cause of death is still unknown and now unrecoverable.

A run that can die must leave a body. run-epic should write its own log under --state-root (rotating, one file per run id) carrying stderr and any panic, independent of how the operator redirected the process. An operator launching a run should not have to remember to capture output for the run to be diagnosable.

Acceptance: a test that panics a run asserts the panic text is present in the run's own log file under the state root.
acceptance_criteria: run-epic writes stderr and any panic to a log under --state-root regardless of process redirection; a test asserts a panicking run leaves its panic text in that file
